newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-VETERAN VIERCHOWOD TO MAKE DEBUT FOR MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VETERAN VIERCHOWOD TO MAKE DEBUT FOR MILAN.

text.p: The 37-year-old Pietro Vierchowod, the oldest player in Italy's Serie A, makes his debut for champions AC Milan this weekend on the opening day of the Italian league season.

Vierchowod, who has played 555 Italian league games in 19 seasons of first-class soccer, was a surprise midweek addition to the Milan squad as a temporary replacement for another veteran, 36-year-old Franco Baresi, who injured an ankle in last Sunday's 2-0 Italian Cup win over Empoli.

In mid-summer Vierchowod moved from European champions Juventus to newly promoted Perugia on a free transfer but subsequent differences with Perugia coach Giovanni Galeone saw Vierchowod leave the Umbrian club, allowing Milan to pick him up without paying a fee.
Vierchowod is inevitably on a one-year contract with Milan but this week pronounced himself delighted with his new club, commenting: "I would have signed for Milan, even for only six months".

Vierchowod will be partnered by Paolo Maldini, Alessandro Costacurta and Christian Panucci in an otherwise familiar-looking Milan defence for the champions' opening game at home to newly promoted Verona on Sunday.
New Milan coach, Uruguyan Oscar Washington Tabarez, may be tempted to stick to the tried and trusted formation inherited from predecessor Fabio Capello, now with Real Madrid.

This means Dutch signings Edgar Davids and Michael Reiziger are likely to start on the substitutes' bench, while Liberian George Weah, Roberto Baggio and Marco Simone lead the attack with Demetrio Albertini, Frenchman Marcel Desailly and Croat Zvonimir Boban in midfield.
Milan's Montenegrin schemer, Dejan "The Genius" Savicevic, misses the game through suspension.
Italian Cup holders Fiorentina, who began the season on a bright note when defeating Milan 2-1 in the Italian SuperCup two weeks ago, start the season with a home game against Vicenza.

There is no shortage of exciting, and expensive, talent on view, not least at Juventus who unveil their brand new trident attack of Croat Alen Boksic, Christian Vieri and Alessandro Del Piero at newly promted Reggiana.

Mid-summer signings Boksic and Vieri have the difficult task of replacing Gianluca Vialli and Fabrizio Ravanelli, who between them scored 55 league goals for Juventus over the last two seasons before departing for England.
Two other new signings, Frenchman Zinedine Zidane in midfield and Uruguyan Paolo Montero in defence, are also due to make their Juventus league debuts.
Those Italian clubs with UEFA Cup ties next Tuesday, namely Internazionale, AS Roma, Parma and Lazio, all play their opening games on Saturday.

Inter, away to Udinese, are expected to field at least six foreigners - Frenchman Joceyln Angloma in defence, Swiss Ciriaco Sforza, Englishman Paul Ince, Argentine Javier Zanetti and Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff in midfield with Chilean Ivan Zamorano in attack.
Udinese field their own major overseas import in the shape of Germany's European Championship hero, striker Oliver Bierhoff, scorer of 17 league goals last season.
Parma, at home to Napoli, take the wraps off $15 million dollar Enrico Chiesa, ex-Sampdoria and the most expensive buy of the Italian summer.
